    Read a rectangular pixel window of one channel

    Source: R/image-windows.R
    sg_read_window.Rd

    Reads height rows and width columns of one channel plane starting at the 0-based pixel offset (x0, y0). Only the image blocks that cover the window are decoded, so windows of very large whole-slide files are cheap. Parts of the window outside the image are filled with fill, which makes fields at the slide edge keep their nominal size.

    Usage

    sg_read_window(path, channel, x0, y0, width, height = width, fill = 0)

    Arguments

    path

    Path to the image file.

    channel

    Channel number (as in sg_image_channels()) or channel name.

    x0, y0

    0-based column and row of the top-left pixel; may be negative.

    width, height

    Window size in pixels.

    fill

    Value used outside the image.

    Value

    A numeric matrix with height rows and width columns ([y, x]), with attributes x0, y0 and channel (the name).

    See also

    sg_read_field(), sg_image_channels()

    Examples

    f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
plane <- matrix(0:11, nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
invisible(tiff::writeTIFF(plane / 255, f, bits.per.sample = 8L))
sg_read_window(f, 1, x0 = 1, y0 = 0, width = 2, height = 2)
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    2
#> [2,]    5    6
#> attr(,"x0")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,"y0")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,"channel")
#> [1] "ch1"
